q: He was left holding the bag. This means:
e: Be left holding the bag = be left to take the blame alone.

q: We need to touch base before the briefing. “Touch base” means:
e: Touch base = make brief contact.

q: The officer called the shots. This means:
e: To make the decisions.

q: They were caught off guard. This means:
e: Caught off guard = taken by surprise.

q: The report was spot on. This means:
e: Spot on = exactly right.

q: Let's play it by ear. This means:
e: Play it by ear = decide as you go along.

q: He threw in the towel. This means:
e: Throw in the towel = give up.

q: It's a grey area. This means:
e: A grey area (US spelling: gray area) = something not clearly defined.

q: He is out of the loop. This means:
e: To be out of the loop.

q: We are back to square one. This means:
e: Back to square one = back to the starting point, after a plan has failed.

q: That is par for the course. This means:
e: Par for the course: what is normal and expected.

q: He kept me in the dark. This means:
e: To keep someone in the dark.

q: The talks hit a snag. This means:
e: Hit a snag = meet an unexpected problem.

q: They went the extra mile. This means:
e: Go the extra mile = make a special effort.

q: Let's get the ball rolling. This means:
e: Get the ball rolling = start an activity.

q: He is a stickler for detail. This means:
e: A stickler for detail = someone who insists on precision.

q: We will cross that bridge when we come to it.
e: We will deal with that problem later, when it arrives.

q: The briefing was a whistle-stop tour of the region.
e: A whistle-stop tour = a very quick visit or overview.

q: Excessive noise is _____ to concentration.
e: *Harmful to* means damaging to something.

q: Untreated waste is _____ to marine life.
e: *Harmful to* is the standard pattern with living things.

q: Long exposure to the sun can be _____ to the skin.
e: *Harmful* means causing damage.

q: The meeting time is very _____ for the team based in Gabes.
e: *Inconvenient* means awkward or badly timed. Careful: it does not mean improper.

q: Losing my passport the night before departure was extremely _____.
e: *Inconvenient* describes a situation that causes trouble or delay.

q: If this hour is _____, we can meet tomorrow instead.
e: *Inconvenient* means not suitable or not practical.

q: Please _____ that all the windows are closed before you leave.
e: *Ensure that* means make certain that. *Undergo* means to experience.

q: The escort will _____ that the convoy arrives safely.
e: *Ensure* means make certain. *Insure* concerns insurance, *assure* means to reassure a person.

q: Double-check the list to _____ that nothing has been forgotten.
e: *Ensure* is followed by a *that* clause.

q: The earthquake left widespread _____ in the valley.
e: *Devastation* means severe and widespread destruction.

q: The flood caused terrible _____; entire villages disappeared.
e: *Devastation* is the noun for massive damage.

q: Photographs showed the _____ left behind by the fire.
e: *Devastation* refers to the ruin left by a disaster.

q: The witness could not give an _____ account of the incident.
e: *Accurate* means exact and free from error. *Prior* means earlier.

q: We need an _____ estimate, not a rough guess.
e: *Accurate* is the opposite of approximate.

q: The map turned out to be less _____ than we expected.
e: *Accurate* describes something that corresponds exactly to reality.

q: Drowsiness is a common _____ of this treatment.
e: *Side effect* is the fixed term for a secondary and unwanted effect of a medicine.

q: The drug is effective, but its _____ include nausea.
e: *Side effects* are the secondary effects of a treatment.

q: Doctors must warn patients about every possible _____.
e: Only *side effect* refers to medicine.

q: The course is designed to help officers _____ their leadership skills.
e: Skills are *developed*. *Grow* and *stretch* are not used with abilities acquired through training.

q: Reading widely helps students _____ their vocabulary.
e: *Develop a vocabulary* is the standard collocation.

q: The programme aims to _____ practical negotiating skills.
e: *Develop* is the verb used with skills and abilities.

q: The minister has a very _____ schedule this month.
e: *A tight schedule* leaves very little spare time.

q: We are working to a _____ deadline.
e: *A tight deadline* is one that is difficult to meet.

q: With such a _____ programme, there is no room for delay.
e: *Tight* describes a programme with no spare time.

q: On whose _____ was the door opened?
e: *On whose authority* asks who gave the order or the right to act.

q: The guard acted on the _____ of the duty officer.
e: *On the authority of somebody* means with that person's permission.

q: Nobody here has the _____ to release this file.
e: *Authority* is the right or power to act.

q: She suffered from the _____ of the accident for months.
e: *After-effects* are the consequences that persist long after an event.

q: The _____ of the drought were felt for years.
e: *After-effects* describes lasting consequences.

q: Fatigue is one of the lasting _____ of the illness.
e: *After-effects* are the effects that remain once the cause has passed.

q: After eight years in prison, the man was finally _____.
e: *Released* means set free. *Jailed* means the opposite.

q: The hostages were _____ unharmed.
e: *Released* means freed from captivity.

q: He was _____ from custody once the charges were dropped.
e: *Released from custody* means allowed to leave.

q: The writer was _____ from his homeland for his articles.
e: *Exiled* means forced to live outside one's own country. *Evicted* applies to a home.

q: Several opposition figures were _____ after the coup.
e: *Exiled* means banished from the country.

q: He lived in _____ for twenty years before returning.
e: *Exile* is the noun for enforced absence from one's country.
